messages:
pagerduty: PAGER — region: eu-central3 | service: inference-serving | symptom: GPU queue growth + failed scale-ups due to GCP quota errors. Severity: P2. Paging on-call.

oncall-maya: ACK — i'm awake, will triage. queue length jumping, autoscaler showing repeated quota errors. tagging infra.

sre-aaron: seen the spikes in tail latency. 95p token latency up to 4.8s, request queue at ~1200. backend pods are saturated. autoscaler logs show provisioning failing with quota errors from gcp compute API.

infra-sam: confirming: GCP API returning RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / QuotaExceeded for GPUs in region eu-central3. Looks like account-level soft cap hit. Trying to re-run allocation yields: 
```
ERROR: compute.instances.insert failed: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for region 'europe-central3'.
code: 403, reason: QUOTA_EXCEEDED
```

oncall-maya: rough impact? which customers seeing errors?

cs-arthur: multiple customers reporting 429/503s in their dashboards. I pulled customer X and Y — spike in error rate since 3921000000. Escalating proactively.

ops-bot: autoscaler:scale_attempt id=ba7f3 start -> failed (quota). queued_requests=1248, active_gpus=256, desired_gpus=320. fallback_attempts=2.

sre-aaron: immediate mitigation proposals:
- reroute a portion of traffic to us-west2 region where capacity exists (fast but adds latency).
- enable quantized smaller model variant for non-critical inference to reduce GPU need (fallback-model-smallq).
- drain and schedule lower-priority batch tasks to free slots.
None of these require quota increases.

infra-sam: can confirm us-west2 has spare capacity. i'll open a temporary routing rule. need a quick thumbs from product for customer-visible tradeoff.

product-ryan: thumbs for routing to us-west2 (temporary). we should inform customers about increased latency for some requests. prefer targeted routing for lower-SLA tenants first.

oncall-maya: executing plan: 1) add route rule -> 20% of inference traffic to us-west2, weighted by tenant tags (non-enterprise first). 2) enable fallback-model-smallq for high-volume tenants. 3) contact GCP support for quota increase (parallel).

infra-sam: applying route change now. patch: 
```yaml
traffic_shaper:
  - match: tenant_slo != enterprise
    weight: 0.2
    region: us-west2
```
applied. monitoring...

ops-bot: routing update applied. new distribution: eu-central3 80%, us-west2 20%.

sre-aaron: enabling fallback-model-smallq on the inference pool for non-critical requests. won't affect enterprise pinned models.

oncall-maya: quick health check: queue dropped from 1248 -> 610 in 30s after routing. 95p latency down to 2.6s. progress.

cs-arthur: customer X still seeing intermittent 503s for heavy jobs. We should offer workaround: schedule retries or route specific job to us-west2. I'll DM affected customers.

infra-sam: opened a GCP support case (case: 12345678). notes: requesting temporary quota bump for GPUs in europe-central3; provided urgent justification for production traffic. ETA from support unknown.

ops-bot: autoscaler:scale_attempt id=bb8f4 -> success. new active_gpus=288.

sre-aaron: still seeing some throttling from GCP (rate-limited), but overall capacity increasing. keep monitoring for secondary waves.

oncall-maya: next steps: (1) keep routing rule until quota bump or flux subsides; (2) follow up with GCP support hourly; (3) run a brief post-incident impact assessment and notify customers of mitigation and timelines.

product-ryan: ask for a short customer-facing blurb once we have ETA from GCP. cs-arthur can you draft?

cs-arthur: on it. draft will state: brief outage, mitigation (partial reroute), expected recovery actions, recommended customer retries/backoffs.

infra-sam: note for later RCA: need automated early detection for region-level GPU quota exhaustion and an out-of-band routing plan that can flip weighting automatically. filing infra-ticket INFRA-4921.

oncall-maya: thanks team. marking initial pager as handled. will stay in thread until GCP confirms. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: PAGER RESOLVED -> severity de-escalated to P3 at 3921000189. monitoring continues.
